messages:
anya: Heads-up — nightly evals for rwd-open-7b-quant spiked on sample-quality tests after last kernel rollout. Failure rate on the ‘coding-rubric’ prompt set jumped from 2.1% -> 18.4% at 03:02 UTC.
kevin: Oof, which rollout/commit?
anya: Deploy was automated at 02:50 UTC, PR #4823 (commit 1f3b9d2) — attention tile scheduler reorder + small packaging change.
maria: Do we have example outputs?
anya: Pasted a couple below (truncated) — notice sampling loops and repeated token prefixes.
anya: ```
prompt: "Write a short helper to parse CSV lines in python"
baseline (float kernel): "def parse_csv(line):
    parts = line.split(',')
    return [p.strip() for p in parts]"
quant-after (new kernel): "def parse_csv(line):
def parse_csv(line):
def parse_csv(line):
    return line.split(',')
    return line.split(',')
"
```
kevin: That looks like duplicated prefix copy-paste, not truncation. Could be KV-cache or attention matrix shuffle.
sam: eval-bot shows mismatch in token-level transition probabilities for early tokens (steps 1-10). I can dump logits for a failing example.
eval-bot: Attached: /evals/nightly/1826123456/rwd-open-7b-quant/logits-diff-1.json (summary: KL divergence spike 12x at step 3-7 for top-5).
maria: I want to check RNG/seed handling across quantized kernels — any change there?
anya: PR touched scheduling only, but the new fused path includes a tiny change to seed advancement in sample loop (line 218 in sampler.cu).
kevin: @anya can you grep the sampler change?
anya: snippet: ```
- // advance rng after gather
- rng.advance(n)
+ // advance rng before gather for better tile alignment
+ rng.advance(n)
```
kevin: Hmm that looks functionally same but ordering might interact with tiled attention prefetch. Could cause off-by-one in RNG state used by top-k sampling.
maria: Another hypothesis: the reordering introduced different memory aliasing which breaks in-place KV updates for quantized weights. Any crash logs?
anya: No segfaults. Just bad generations. Also seeing an uptick in 502s at 02:51 but they resolved after autoscale.
sam: I ran a short A/B: floating kernels (old) vs quantized+new-scheduler (current). Deterministic seed pair shows outputs diverge at token 3 consistently.
eval-bot: Metric snapshot: pre-rollout pass@1=0.87, post-rollout pass@1=0.71 on coding-rubric. Repeat-rate (consecutive tokens equal) increased from 0.8% -> 9.6%.
kevin: Steps: 1) revert scheduler on a canary pool and re-run failing subset, 2) bisect sampler commit if revert fixes it. Who can run canary?
maria: I can stand up a small canary on dedicated-gpu-2, but need a rollout tag. What's a safe rollback tag?
anya: Rollback tag is release/2026-03-19-hotfix (pre-PR4823). I can kick it.
kevin: I'll prepare a minimal bisect plan and add an eval harness to capture token-level RNG state, logits, and KV cache snapshots for the first 8 tokens. Need that to confirm off-by-one.
anya: Doing the canary now. Kicking a purge + redeploy to dedicated-gpu-2.
deploy-bot: [02:58 UTC] Started redeploy of model rwd-open-7b-quant to host dedicated-gpu-2 with tag release/2026-03-19-hotfix.
anya: Canary finished — quick eval: pass@1 back to 0.86 for the subset, repeat-rate down to 1.0%.
kevin: That strongly implicates the scheduler reorder. Good rollback for now. We'll keep the PR open and add unit tests for RNG ordering + a CI eval that runs token-by-token diffs between float and quantized sampling paths.
maria: I'll file an infra ticket to add the KV-cache snapshot capability to debug future regressions.
sam: +1. Also adding an eval that samples with multiple alignment seeds to catch early token divergence.
anya: Filed ticket RD-937 (KV snapshot), PR for bisect plan in my fork: https://git.internal/rw/eng-runtime/pulls/4890
kevin: Nice. Postmortem action items: - revert to hotfix release until merged tests, - add RNG-order unit test, - add nightly diff alert for token-level KL jumps.
maria: Assigning owners: kevin -> tests, anya -> rollback/PR, sam -> evals alerting, maria -> infra ticket.
anya: Thanks all. Will follow up with diffs and logs in the PR. :thumbsup:
